newsitem.title: ITALY: BankItaly foreign currency reserves $35bln - Fazio.
newsitem.headline: BankItaly foreign currency reserves $35bln - Fazio.

text.p: The Bank of Italy's foreign currency reserves stood at $35 billion on Friday while foreign currency denominated net assets were $45 billion at end 1996.

"Yesterday the foreign currency reserves of the Bank of Italy and the Italian currency exchange office stood at $35 billlion after setting aside 21 billion for official Ecu repurchases, repurchase operations and other short term liabilities," Fazio said in a speech at a forex conference.
"Foreign currency denominated net assets, excluding gold, rose from $28 billion on December 31, 1993 to $45 billion at the end of 1996," he said.
Fazio said that in the whole of 1996 the current account balance of payments showed a surplus of around 70 trillion lire, confirming a growth trend.
These two elements, reserves and the surplus, made a "solid base for maintaining internal and external stability of our currency," he said.

He added the lira's appreciation in the last 18 months and its re-entry into Europe's exchange rate mechanism late last year allowed Italian companies to keep a competitive advantage of 10 percent in respect to lira levels in the first half of 1992, before it was forced out of the ERM.
He noted the lira's exchange rate on Friday was five percent higher than that in December 1994, with an appreciation of 25 percent in respect of the historic lows touched in March 1995.
